title: Modified Duke Criteria — Infective Endocarditis
keywords: definite = 2 major or 1 major plus 3 minor or 5 minor
possible = 1 major plus 1 minor or 3 minor
typical IE organisms viridans strep staph aureus HACEK enterococcus
vegetation new regurgitation are the two major criteria buckets
predisposition fever vascular immunologic microbiologic are the five minor criteria
sources: Li JS, Sexton DJ, Mick N, et al. Proposed modifications to the Duke criteria for the diagnosis of infective endocarditis. Clin Infect Dis. 2000;30(4):633-638.

Fowler VG, Durack DT, Selton-Suty C, et al. The 2023 Duke-ISCVID Criteria for Infective Endocarditis — Updated Modification of the Duke Criteria. Clin Infect Dis. 2023 (advanced-imaging and additional-pathogen refinements to the framework below; the core major/minor structure and combination logic are unchanged from 2000).

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap. Built as a structured reference rather than a numeric calculator: the Definite/Possible/Rejected classification is combinatorial (different major+minor combinations meet 'definite' at different total counts), not a single point-threshold, so a scored calculator would misrepresent it.

summary: Classifies a suspected infective endocarditis case as Definite, Possible, or Rejected from major and minor clinical/microbiologic/echocardiographic criteria — not a point score, a specific combination rule.
whyThisMatters: Infective endocarditis has no single confirmatory test — the diagnosis is made by pattern-matching microbiology, imaging, and clinical findings against this framework, and getting the combination logic right (rather than eyeballing 'enough criteria') is what separates a confident diagnosis from a missed or over-called one.
clinicalTakeaway: Two major criteria, or one major plus three minor, or five minor = Definite. One major plus one minor, or three minor = Possible. Below that — or a firm alternative diagnosis, or resolution within four days of antibiotics — is Rejected. Get blood cultures before antibiotics whenever feasible; the major microbiologic criterion depends on it.

items: Typical IE organism from 2 separate blood cultures: viridans streptococci, Streptococcus gallolyticus (bovis), HACEK group, Staphylococcus aureus, or community-acquired enterococci without a primary focus.
OR a non-typical organism persistently positive: ≥ 2 positive cultures drawn > 12 h apart, or all of 3 (or a majority of ≥ 4) separate cultures with the first and last drawn ≥ 1 h apart.
OR a single positive culture for Coxiella burnetii, or a phase I IgG antibody titer > 1:800.

Echocardiogram positive for IE: an oscillating intracardiac mass on a valve or supporting structure, an abscess, or new partial dehiscence of a prosthetic valve. (The 2023 Duke-ISCVID update also recognizes cardiac CT and PET/CT findings for prosthetic valve endocarditis, where TEE is often limited.)
OR new valvular regurgitation — a worsening or changing pre-existing murmur is NOT sufficient on its own.
Predisposition: a predisposing heart condition (prosthetic valve, prior IE, most congenital/valvular disease) or injection drug use.
Vascular phenomena: major arterial emboli, septic pulmonary infarcts, mycotic aneurysm, intracranial hemorrhage, conjunctival hemorrhages, Janeway lesions.
Immunologic phenomena: glomerulonephritis, Osler nodes, Roth spots, positive rheumatoid factor.
Microbiological evidence not meeting a major criterion: a positive blood culture not qualifying above, or serologic evidence of active infection with an organism consistent with IE.

rows: 2 major — OR — 1 major + 3 minor — OR — 5 minor

A firm alternate diagnosis explains the findings; OR resolution of the syndrome with ≤ 4 days of antibiotics; OR no pathologic evidence of IE at surgery or autopsy after ≤ 4 days of antibiotics; OR simply doesn't meet the 'Possible' criteria above

body.text: Draw blood cultures BEFORE starting antibiotics whenever the patient is stable enough to allow it — three sets from separate venipuncture sites is standard practice. Empiric antibiotics started before cultures are drawn is the most common preventable reason the major microbiologic criterion can't later be met.
